bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to housing; prohibiting private equity company ownership of single-family homes; providing attorney general enforcement; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 500.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[500.50] SINGLE-FAMILY HOMES; PRIVATE EQUITY OWNERSHIP PROHIBITED.

Subdivision 1.

Definitions.

(a) For purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given.

(b) "Private equity company" means an investor or group of investors who primarily engage in the raising or returning of capital and who invest, develop, or dispose of specified assets. A private equity company includes publicly or nonpublicly traded entities, real estate investment trusts, and any investment firm that buys and manages private companies to make a profit. A private equity company does not include any of the following:

(1) a local, state, or federal unit of government or agency;

(2) a land trust as defined in section 462A.31;

(3) a nonprofit organized under chapter 317A that is creating, rehabilitating, or providing affordable housing to low- and moderate-income renters or home buyers;

(4) a corporation primarily engaged in housing development through the construction and rehabilitation of single-family homes; or

(5) a mortgage note holder that owns the single-family homes through foreclosure.

(c) "Homestead" means a property classified as class 1a under section 273.13, subdivision 22.

(d) "Real estate investment trust" has the meaning given in United States Code, title 26, section 856.

(e) "Single-family home" means a residential property consisting of one to four dwelling units.

Subd. 2.

Single-family homes; private equity ownership prohibition.

A private equity company is prohibited from having a direct or indirect ownership interest in a single-family home. This subdivision does not prohibit a natural person from acquiring an ownership interest in a home that is classified as homestead property for tax purposes.

Subd. 3.

Enforcement.

The attorney general may enforce this section pursuant to section 8.31.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

This section is effective August 1, 2026, and applies to interests in real property acquired on or after that date.
